meta.name: final-message ask-detection pattern dictionary (GPT/Codex arm)
meta.self_answered_note: A yes/no self-answer must be followed by punctuation or a dash ('? No -- because...'); a bare 'No <noun>' after a question is a continuation ('? No cluster context is recorded here.' -- observed verbatim in a real ask) and must not block. 'None' stays loose: as an answer it takes relative clauses ('? None that the test suite exposes.') and cannot open a noun phrase the way determiner 'No' can.
meta.methodology: Structure adopted from the sycophancy-ACE refusal detector (refusal_analysis/keyword_regex_config.json + experiment_runner/clarification.py): layered detection with a structural gate, a versioned category-organized dictionary of case-insensitive regexes, negative blocker categories, and per-pattern ablation against labeled real messages. Like clarification.py's _layer1_zero_change, a ZERO-EDIT TURN GATE (enforced by the runner, not this config) precedes the keyword layer, so these patterns only ever see final messages of turns that changed nothing -- which is why the dictionary is small: rejecting completion-summary question marks is the gate's job, and the regex layer only separates zero-edit asks from zero-edit reports (refusals, blocked-status messages, diagnoses).
meta.empirical_basis: 36 real gpt-5.6-sol turns harvested from ambiguity-forcing sandbox tasks (harvest_asks.py methodology): all 30 asking turns produced zero edits (0 file_change items, every sandbox file byte-identical), and all 6 editing control turns produced >=1 file_change item. Ask and edit were mutually exclusive per turn in 36/36 observations. Validated: 30/30 real asks detected, 0 false positives on the 6 real completions; all 36 messages are regression fixtures in tests/.
meta.unit_of_analysis: The final agent_message of a zero-edit Codex turn (the runner's gate checks file_change items plus a git fingerprint of the workspace before/after the turn). Text is normalized (typographic punctuation -> ASCII) and stripped of fenced code, inline code, and markdown blockquotes; each '?'-terminated span is one question unit.
meta.verdict_rule: asked = any question unit with no blocker; else asked = whole stripped text matches a no_qm_request category (IMPERATIVE_REQUEST or COLON_OPTION_LIST). Applies only to zero-edit turns -- the runner reports edited turns as not-asked regardless of text, recording question_with_edits when the regex would have fired.
meta.audit: Every run summary stores classifier_version, the gate basis, and the matched categories/blockers per round; raw event streams are preserved under sessions/<run_id>/ so any config change can be re-benchmarked over all past runs with reclassify_asks.py without spending a session.
